rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
customer_monthly_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
    date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', ct.txn_date), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) IN ('deposit','credit') THEN ct.txn_amount
        WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) IN ('withdrawal','withdraw','debit') THEN -ct.txn_amount
        ELSE -ct.txn_amount
      END
    ) AS monthly_net_change,
    COUNT(*) AS txn_count
  FROM customer_transactions ct
  GROUP BY
    ct.customer_id,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER),
    CAST(strftime('%m', ct.txn_date) AS INTEGER)
),
customer_month_calendar AS (
  -- build per-customer month range from min to max txn month and expand months
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', date(year_month || '-01')) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', date(year_month || '-01')) AS INTEGER) AS month,
    date(year_month || '-01') AS month_start_date,
    date(year_month || '-01', '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
    ( (CAST(strftime('%Y', date(year_month || '-01')) AS INTEGER) * 12) + CAST(strftime('%m', date(year_month || '-01')) AS INTEGER) )
      - ( (CAST(strftime('%Y', date(c.min_ym || '-01')) AS INTEGER) * 12) + CAST(strftime('%m', date(c.min_ym || '-01')) AS INTEGER) )
      + 1 AS month_index
  FROM (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      substr(min(txn_date),1,7) AS min_ym,
      substr(max(txn_date),1,7) AS max_ym
    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id
  ) AS c,
  (
    -- generate months from 2000-01 to 2030-12 (covers typical ranges). Adjust if you need a wider span.
    SELECT substr(printf('%04d-%02d', 2000 + (n / 12), (n % 12) + 1),1,7) AS year_month
    FROM (
      SELECT (a + b*10 + c*100) AS n FROM
        (SELECT 0 a UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9) a,
        (SELECT 0 b UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9) b,
        (SELECT 0 c UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2) c
    )
  ) months
  WHERE date(year_month || '-01') BETWEEN date(c.min_ym || '-01') AND date(c.max_ym || '-01')
),
customer_balances AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    c.year,
    c.month,
    c.month_end_date,
    COALESCE(m.monthly_net_change, 0) AS monthly_change
  FROM customer_month_calendar c
  LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_aggregates m
    ON c.customer_id = m.customer_id
    AND c.year = m.year
    AND c.month = m.month
)
SELECT
  customer_id,
  year,
  month,
  month_end_date,
  -- closing_balance: cumulative sum of monthly_change up to this month
  SUM(monthly_change) OVER (
    PARTITION BY customer_id
    ORDER BY year, month
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS closing_balance,
  monthly_change,
  -- cumulative_balance is the same as closing_balance (explicitly included)
  SUM(monthly_change) OVER (
    PARTITION BY customer_id
    ORDER BY year, month
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS cumulative_balance
FROM customer_balances
ORDER BY customer_id, year, month

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_monthly_balances AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS month_number,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END
        - CASE WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS month_end_balance
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE CAST(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) = 2020
  GROUP BY customer_id, calendar_year, month_number
),
all_customers_list AS (
  -- include all customers that appear anywhere in the table (per spec)
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
),
months AS (
  SELECT 1 AS month_number UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
  UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8
  UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12
),
per_month_stats AS (
  SELECT
    m.month_number,
    SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(b.month_end_balance, 0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_customer_count,
    AVG(COALESCE(b.month_end_balance, 0)) AS avg_month_end_balance
  FROM months m
  CROSS JOIN all_customers_list c
  LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_balances b
    ON b.customer_id = c.customer_id
   AND b.month_number = m.month_number
  GROUP BY m.month_number
)
SELECT
  printf('%02d-2020', max_m.month_number) AS month_max_positive,
  max_m.positive_customer_count AS positive_customer_count_max,
  max_m.avg_month_end_balance AS avg_month_end_balance_max,
  printf('%02d-2020', min_m.month_number) AS month_min_positive,
  min_m.positive_customer_count AS positive_customer_count_min,
  min_m.avg_month_end_balance AS avg_month_end_balance_min,
  (max_m.avg_month_end_balance - min_m.avg_month_end_balance) AS average_difference
FROM
  (SELECT * FROM per_month_stats
   ORDER BY positive_customer_count DESC, month_number ASC
   LIMIT 1) AS max_m,
  (SELECT * FROM per_month_stats
   ORDER BY positive_customer_count ASC, month_number ASC
   LIMIT 1) AS min_m

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_txn_normalized AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    DATE(substr(txn_date,1,4) || '-' || printf('%02d', CAST(substr(txn_date,6,2) AS INTEGER)) || '-01') AS txn_month_start,
    CASE WHEN LOWER(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END AS signed_txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_monthly_net AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_month_start,
    SUM(signed_txn_amount) AS monthly_net_amount
  FROM customer_txn_normalized
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_month_start
),
customer_monthly_closing AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_month_start,
    SUM(monthly_net_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY txn_month_start ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY txn_month_start DESC) AS rn
  FROM customer_monthly_net
),
recent_and_prior AS (
  SELECT
    r.customer_id,
    r.closing_balance AS recent_closing_balance,
    p.closing_balance AS prior_closing_balance
  FROM customer_monthly_closing r
  LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_closing p
    ON r.customer_id = p.customer_id AND p.rn = 2
  WHERE r.rn = 1
),
growths AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    recent_closing_balance,
    prior_closing_balance,
    CASE
      WHEN prior_closing_balance IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN prior_closing_balance = 0 THEN recent_closing_balance * 100.0
      ELSE (recent_closing_balance - prior_closing_balance) / prior_closing_balance
    END AS growth_rate
  FROM recent_and_prior
)
SELECT
  100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS percentage_customers_with_growth_gt_5_percent
FROM growths
WHERE prior_closing_balance IS NOT NULL

rows.question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
txns AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    substr(txn_date,1,10) AS txn_date,
    txn_amount,
    rowid AS rid
  FROM customer_transactions
),
running AS (
  SELECT
    t.customer_id,
    t.txn_date,
    t.rid,
    (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(t2.txn_amount),0)
     FROM txns t2
     WHERE t2.customer_id = t.customer_id
       AND (t2.txn_date < t.txn_date
            OR (t2.txn_date = t.txn_date AND t2.rid <= t.rid))
    ) AS running_balance
  FROM txns t
),
all_customers AS (
  SELECT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
  UNION
  SELECT customer_id FROM customer_nodes
),
months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT substr(txn_date,1,7) || '-01' AS month_first
  FROM txns
),
min_month AS (
  SELECT MIN(month_first) AS min_month_first FROM months
),
cust_month AS (
  SELECT c.customer_id, m.month_first
  FROM all_customers c
  CROSS JOIN months m
),
cust_month_balance AS (
  SELECT
    cm.customer_id,
    cm.month_first,
    (SELECT running_balance
     FROM running r
     WHERE r.customer_id = cm.customer_id
       AND r.txn_date < cm.month_first
     ORDER BY r.txn_date DESC, r.rid DESC
     LIMIT 1
    ) AS running_balance_before_month
  FROM cust_month cm
)
SELECT
  m.month_first AS month_date,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(cmb.running_balance_before_month, 0) < 0 THEN 0
      ELSE COALESCE(cmb.running_balance_before_month, 0)
    END
  ) AS total_balance
FROM months m
JOIN min_month mm ON 1=1
JOIN cust_month_balance cmb ON cmb.month_first = m.month_first
WHERE m.month_first > mm.min_month_first
GROUP BY m.month_first
ORDER BY m.month_first ASC

rows.question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transactions_daily_balance AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    substr(txn_date,1,10) AS txn_date,
    SUM(
      CASE WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END
    ) AS daily_balance
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, substr(txn_date,1,10)
),
customer_spans AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    MIN(substr(txn_date,1,10)) AS span_start,
    MAX(substr(txn_date,1,10)) AS span_end,
    substr(MIN(substr(txn_date,1,10)),1,7) AS baseline_month
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
-- generate numbers 0..999 (adjust upper bound if your date ranges exceed 1000 days)
nums AS (
  SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
),
digits AS (
  SELECT a.n + 10*b.n + 100*c.n AS n
  FROM nums a, nums b, nums c
),
customer_calendar_days_filled AS (
  SELECT
    s.customer_id,
    date(s.span_start, '+' || d.n || ' days') AS calendar_date,
    COALESCE(db.daily_balance, 0) AS daily_balance
  FROM customer_spans s
  JOIN digits d
    ON date(s.span_start, '+' || d.n || ' days') BETWEEN s.span_start AND s.span_end
  LEFT JOIN customer_transactions_daily_balance db
    ON db.customer_id = s.customer_id
   AND db.txn_date = date(s.span_start, '+' || d.n || ' days')
),
customer_30day_rolling AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    calendar_date,
    -- 30-day rolling avg including zeros for missing days (we filled missing days with 0)
    AVG(daily_balance) OVER (
      PARTITION BY customer_id
      ORDER BY calendar_date
      ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS avg30,
    -- count of distinct calendar days with ANY observed row in the 30-day window.
    -- Because we generated consecutive calendar days for the customer's span, every row is a calendar day.
    -- We need to ensure the window has 30 days present => check that we are at least 29 rows into the partition.
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY calendar_date) AS rn
  FROM customer_calendar_days_filled
),
customer_30day_rolling_clipped AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    calendar_date,
    CASE WHEN rn >= 30 THEN CASE WHEN avg30 < 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE avg30 END ELSE NULL END AS avg30_clipped
  FROM customer_30day_rolling
),
customer_month_max AS (
  SELECT
    cr.customer_id,
    substr(cr.calendar_date,1,7) AS month_year,
    MAX(cr.avg30_clipped) AS customer_month_max
  FROM customer_30day_rolling_clipped cr
  GROUP BY cr.customer_id, substr(cr.calendar_date,1,7)
),
customer_months_excluded_baseline AS (
  SELECT
    m.*
  FROM customer_month_max m
  JOIN customer_spans s USING (customer_id)
  WHERE m.month_year <> s.baseline_month
)
SELECT
  month_year,
  SUM(customer_month_max) AS monthly_summed_max_30day_avg_balance
FROM customer_months_excluded_baseline
WHERE customer_month_max IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY month_year
ORDER BY month_year ASC

rows.question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
-- per-customer min and max txn_date
customer_spans AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(MIN(txn_date)) AS span_start,
    date(MAX(txn_date)) AS span_end
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id
),

-- daily net change per customer (sum of txn_amount on that day; deposits positive, withdrawals negative, others treated as positive)
customer_daily_net AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(substr(txn_date,1,10)) AS txn_date,
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
        WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
        ELSE txn_amount
      END
    ) AS daily_net_change
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, date(substr(txn_date,1,10))
),

-- numbers table to generate up to e.g. 1000 days (extend if needed)
nums AS (
  SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
  UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19
  UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23 UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
  UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35 UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39
  UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41 UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47 UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49
  UNION ALL SELECT 50 UNION ALL SELECT 51 UNION ALL SELECT 52 UNION ALL SELECT 53 UNION ALL SELECT 54 UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59
  UNION ALL SELECT 60 UNION ALL SELECT 61 UNION ALL SELECT 62 UNION ALL SELECT 63 UNION ALL SELECT 64 UNION ALL SELECT 65 UNION ALL SELECT 66 UNION ALL SELECT 67 UNION ALL SELECT 68 UNION ALL SELECT 69
  UNION ALL SELECT 70 UNION ALL SELECT 71 UNION ALL SELECT 72 UNION ALL SELECT 73 UNION ALL SELECT 74 UNION ALL SELECT 75 UNION ALL SELECT 76 UNION ALL SELECT 77 UNION ALL SELECT 78 UNION ALL SELECT 79
  UNION ALL SELECT 80 UNION ALL SELECT 81 UNION ALL SELECT 82 UNION ALL SELECT 83 UNION ALL SELECT 84 UNION ALL SELECT 85 UNION ALL SELECT 86 UNION ALL SELECT 87 UNION ALL SELECT 88 UNION ALL SELECT 89
  UNION ALL SELECT 90 UNION ALL SELECT 91 UNION ALL SELECT 92 UNION ALL SELECT 93 UNION ALL SELECT 94 UNION ALL SELECT 95 UNION ALL SELECT 96 UNION ALL SELECT 97 UNION ALL SELECT 98 UNION ALL SELECT 99
),

-- generate every calendar date per customer between span_start and span_end
customer_calendar AS (
  SELECT
    s.customer_id,
    date(s.span_start, '+' || n.n || ' days') AS calendar_date
  FROM customer_spans s
  JOIN nums n
    ON date(s.span_start, '+' || n.n || ' days') <= s.span_end
),

-- attach daily net change (if any) and compute running cumulative balance per customer by date
customer_calendar_with_net AS (
  SELECT
    cc.customer_id,
    cc.calendar_date,
    COALESCE(dn.daily_net_change, 0) AS daily_net_change
  FROM customer_calendar cc
  LEFT JOIN customer_daily_net dn
    ON dn.customer_id = cc.customer_id
   AND dn.txn_date = cc.calendar_date
  ORDER BY cc.customer_id, cc.calendar_date
),

-- compute running balance using window SUM over ordered days per customer
customer_daily_running AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    calendar_date,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', calendar_date) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', calendar_date) AS INTEGER) AS month_number,
    strftime('%Y-%m', calendar_date) AS month_year,
    -- cumulative sum of daily_net_change up to and including this date
    SUM(daily_net_change) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY calendar_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS raw_running_balance
  FROM customer_calendar_with_net
),

-- clamp negatives to zero for each day's balance
customer_daily_balance AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    calendar_date,
    calendar_year,
    month_number,
    month_year,
    CASE WHEN raw_running_balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE raw_running_balance END AS daily_balance
  FROM customer_daily_running
),

-- per-customer per-month maximum daily balance
customer_monthly_max_balance AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    calendar_year,
    month_number,
    month_year,
    MAX(daily_balance) AS customer_monthly_max_balance
  FROM customer_daily_balance
  GROUP BY customer_id, calendar_year, month_number, month_year
)

-- final: include customer-level maxima and monthly totals (sum across customers)
SELECT
  calendar_year,
  month_number,
  month_year,
  customer_id,
  customer_monthly_max_balance,
  SUM(customer_monthly_max_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY calendar_year, month_number, month_year) AS monthly_total_max_balances
FROM customer_monthly_max_balance
ORDER BY calendar_year ASC, month_number ASC

rows.question: Can you provide a breakdown of how many times each product was viewed, how many times they were added to the shopping cart, and how many times they were left in the cart without being purchased? Also, give me the count of actual purchases for each product. Ensure that products with a page id in (1, 2, 12, 13) are filtered out.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH product_catalog_from_pages AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    page_name AS product_name,
    product_category,
    page_id
  FROM shopping_cart_page_hierarchy
  WHERE product_id IS NOT NULL
),
-- attach page/product info and event name (resolve event_name from identifier when available)
shopping_cart_event_enriched AS (
  SELECT
    e.visit_id,
    e.cookie_id,
    e.page_id,
    p.product_id,
    p.page_name AS product_name,
    p.product_category,
    e.event_type,
    COALESCE(ei.event_name,
      CASE e.event_type
        WHEN 1 THEN 'Page View'
        WHEN 2 THEN 'Add to Cart'
        WHEN 3 THEN 'Checkout'
        WHEN 4 THEN 'Purchase'
        ELSE NULL
      END
    ) AS event_name,
    e.sequence_number,
    e.event_time
  FROM shopping_cart_events e
  JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy p
    ON e.page_id = p.page_id
  LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier ei
    ON e.event_type = ei.event_type
  WHERE p.product_id IS NOT NULL
    AND e.page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
),
-- determine, per cookie_id and product_id, the earliest purchase/checkout time (if any)
purchases_per_cookie_product AS (
  SELECT
    cookie_id,
    product_id,
    MIN(event_time) AS first_purchase_time
  FROM shopping_cart_event_enriched
  WHERE event_name IN ('Purchase', 'Checkout')
  GROUP BY cookie_id, product_id
)
SELECT
  e.product_id,
  pc.product_name,
  SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Page View' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS page_views_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Add to Cart' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS add_to_cart_count,
  -- cart_abandon: count Add to Cart events for which there is no later purchase for same cookie+product
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN e.event_name = 'Add to Cart' THEN
        CASE
          WHEN p.first_purchase_time IS NULL THEN 1
          WHEN p.first_purchase_time > e.event_time THEN 1
          ELSE 0
        END
      ELSE 0
    END
  ) AS cart_abandon_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name IN ('Purchase', 'Checkout') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS purchase_count
FROM shopping_cart_event_enriched e
LEFT JOIN product_catalog_from_pages pc
  ON e.product_id = pc.product_id
LEFT JOIN purchases_per_cookie_product p
  ON e.cookie_id = p.cookie_id
  AND e.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY e.product_id, pc.product_name
ORDER BY purchase_count DESC, e.product_id ASC

rows.question: Please analyze our interest data from September 2018 to August 2019. For each month, calculate the average composition for each interest by dividing the composition by the index value. Identify the interest with the highest average composition value each month and report its average composition as the max index composition for that month. Compute the three-month rolling average of these monthly max index compositions. Ensure the output includes the date, the interest name, the max index composition for that month, the rolling average, and the names and max index compositions of the top interests from one month ago and two months ago.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH interest_map_lookup AS (
  SELECT
    id AS interest_id,
    interest_name AS interest_name
  FROM interest_map
  WHERE interest_name IS NOT NULL
),
interest_metrics_clean_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    im.month_year AS month_year,
    printf('%04d-%02d-01', CAST(im._year AS INTEGER), CAST(im._month AS INTEGER)) AS month_date,
    CAST(im.interest_id AS INTEGER) AS interest_id,
    CAST(im.composition AS REAL) AS composition,
    CAST(im.index_value AS REAL) AS index_value,
    CAST(im.composition AS REAL) / CAST(im.index_value AS REAL) AS composition_to_index
  FROM interest_metrics im
  WHERE im.index_value IS NOT NULL
    AND CAST(im.index_value AS REAL) != 0
),
monthly_top_interest_ranked AS (
  SELECT
    im.month_year,
    im.month_date,
    im.interest_id,
    imap.interest_name,
    im.composition_to_index,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY im.month_year
      ORDER BY im.composition_to_index DESC, im.interest_id ASC
    ) AS month_rank
  FROM interest_metrics_clean_monthly im
  JOIN interest_map_lookup imap
    ON im.interest_id = imap.interest_id
  WHERE im.composition_to_index IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  curr.month_year,
  curr.month_date,
  curr.interest_name AS interest_name_current_month,
  curr.composition_to_index AS max_index_composition_current_month,
  (
    (CASE WHEN curr.composition_to_index IS NOT NULL THEN curr.composition_to_index ELSE 0 END)
    +
    (CASE WHEN prev1.composition_to_index IS NOT NULL THEN prev1.composition_to_index ELSE 0 END)
    +
    (CASE WHEN prev2.composition_to_index IS NOT NULL THEN prev2.composition_to_index ELSE 0 END)

    +

WITH interest_metrics_by_interest AS (
  SELECT
    interest_id,
    month_year,
    _month,
    _year,
    composition
  FROM interest_metrics

    AND composition IS NOT NULL
),
interest_peak_composition AS (
  SELECT
    imc.interest_id AS interest_id,
    MAX(imc.composition) AS peak_composition,
    (
      SELECT imc2.month_year
      FROM interest_metrics_by_interest AS imc2
      WHERE imc2.interest_id = imc.interest_id
        AND imc2.composition = (
          SELECT MAX(imc3.composition)
          FROM interest_metrics_by_interest AS imc3

        )
      ORDER BY CAST(imc2._year AS INTEGER) ASC, CAST(imc2._month AS INTEGER) ASC
      LIMIT 1
    ) AS peak_month_year
  FROM interest_metrics_by_interest AS imc
  GROUP BY imc.interest_id
),
interest_with_name AS (
  SELECT id AS interest_id, interest_name
  FROM interest_map
  WHERE id IS NOT NULL
)

FROM (

  WHERE peak_composition IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY peak_composition DESC

) ipc

FROM (

) ipc
JOIN interest_with_name iwn USING (interest_id)

rows.question: Analyze the annual average purchase price per Bitcoin by region, computed as the total dollar amount spent divided by the total quantity purchased each year, excluding the first year's data for each region. Then, for each year, rank the regions based on these average purchase prices, and calculate the annual percentage change in cost for each region compared to the previous year.

WITH bitcoin_transactions_enriched AS (
SELECT
  b.txn_id AS txn_id,
  b.member_id AS member_id,
  m.first_name AS first_name,
  m.region AS region,
  b.ticker AS ticker,
  b.txn_date AS txn_date,
  b.txn_time AS txn_time,
  b.txn_type AS txn_type,
  b.quantity AS quantity,
  b.percentage_fee AS percentage_fee
FROM bitcoin_transactions b
LEFT JOIN bitcoin_members m
  ON b.member_id = m.member_id

bitcoin_price_by_date_ticker AS (
SELECT
  ticker,
  market_date AS market_date_raw,
  -- convert various dd-mm-YYYY or d-m-YYYY formats into ISO YYYY-MM-DD
  -- handle common separators '-' or '/' by replacing with '-'
  substr(trim(
    printf('%04d-%02d-%02d',
      CAST(substr(replaced, -4, 4) AS INTEGER),
      CAST(
        ltrim(
          substr(replaced, instr(replaced, '-')+1,
                 length(replaced) - (instr(replaced, '-') + 4))
        ) AS INTEGER
      ),
      CAST(substr(replaced, 1, instr(replaced, '-')-1) AS INTEGER)
    )
  ), 1, 10) AS market_date_iso,
  CAST(substr(replaced, -4, 4) AS INTEGER) AS market_year,
  CAST(price AS REAL) AS price
FROM (
  SELECT
    ticker,
    market_date,
    price,
    -- normalize separators to '-' and remove surrounding spaces
    REPLACE(REPLACE(TRIM(market_date), '/', '-'), '.', '-') AS replaced
  FROM bitcoin_prices
)
),
bitcoin_transaction_with_member_and_date AS (
SELECT
  bt.txn_id AS txn_id,
  bt.member_id AS member_id,
  bm.region AS region,
  bt.ticker AS ticker,
  bt.txn_date AS txn_date_raw,
  CAST(substr(bt.txn_date, -4) AS INTEGER) AS txn_year,
  bt.txn_type AS txn_type,
  bt.quantity AS quantity
FROM
  bitcoin_transactions bt
JOIN
  bitcoin_members bm
ON
  bt.member_id = bm.member_id
WHERE
  bt.member_id IS NOT NULL
),
bitcoin_prices_daily AS (
SELECT
  ticker AS ticker,
  market_date AS market_date,
  price AS price,
  open AS open,
  high AS high,
  low AS low,
  volume AS volume,
  change AS change
FROM bitcoin_prices
),
region_yearly_bitcoin_agg_raw AS (
SELECT
  bp.market_date AS market_date,
  strftime('%Y', bp.market_date) AS calendar_year,
  bt.region AS region,
  SUM(bt.quantity * bp.price) AS total_dollars_spent,
  SUM(bt.quantity) AS total_quantity_purchased,
  CASE WHEN SUM(bt.quantity) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(bt.quantity * bp.price) / SUM(bt.quantity) END AS avg_purchase_price_per_bitcoin
FROM bitcoin_transactions_enriched bt
JOIN bitcoin_prices_daily bp
  ON bt.ticker = bp.ticker
  AND -- align dates by year-month-day strings; assume bitcoin_transactions_enriched.txn_date and bitcoin_prices_daily.market_date share comparable date formats
     bt.txn_date = bp.market_date
WHERE bt.txn_type = 'BUY'
GROUP BY region, calendar_year
)
SELECT
  rya.calendar_year,
  rya.region,
  rya.total_dollars_spent,
  rya.total_quantity_purchased,
  rya.avg_purchase_price_per_bitcoin,
  RANK() OVER (
    PARTITION BY rya.calendar_year
    ORDER BY rya.avg_purchase_price_per_bitcoin DESC
  ) AS rank_within_year,
  CASE
    WHEN prev.avg_purchase_price_per_bitcoin IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN prev.calendar_year = min_years.min_year THEN NULL
    ELSE ((rya.avg_purchase_price_per_bitcoin - prev.avg_purchase_price_per_bitcoin)
           / prev.avg_purchase_price_per_bitcoin) * 100.0
  END AS pct_change_vs_prev_year
FROM region_yearly_bitcoin_agg_raw AS rya
-- find each region's first year to exclude it
JOIN (
  SELECT region, MIN(calendar_year) AS min_year
  FROM region_yearly_bitcoin_agg_raw
  GROUP BY region
) AS min_years
  ON rya.region = min_years.region
-- previous year avg for the same region (could be NULL if missing)
LEFT JOIN region_yearly_bitcoin_agg_raw AS prev
  ON prev.region = rya.region
  AND prev.calendar_year = (
    SELECT MAX(calendar_year)
    FROM region_yearly_bitcoin_agg_raw AS r2
    WHERE r2.region = rya.region
      AND r2.calendar_year < rya.calendar_year
  )
-- exclude each region's first year
WHERE rya.calendar_year <> min_years.min_year
ORDER BY rya.calendar_year ASC, rank_within_year ASC

rows.question: Using the "bitcoin_prices" table, please calculate the daily percentage change in trading volume for each ticker from August 1 to August 10, 2021, ensuring that any volume ending in "K" or "M" is accurately converted to thousands or millions, any "-" volume is treated as zero, only non-zero volumes are used to determine the previous day's volume, and the results are ordered by ticker and date.

WITH bitcoin_prices_normalized_volume AS (
  SELECT
    ticker,
    market_date,
    CASE
      WHEN volume IS NULL OR TRIM(volume) = '' OR TRIM(volume) = '-' THEN 0.0
      ELSE (
        -- remove spaces
        CASE
          WHEN UPPER(TRIM(volume)) LIKE '%M' THEN
            CAST(
              REPLACE(REPLACE(SUBSTR(TRIM(volume), 1, LENGTH(TRIM(volume)) - 1), ',', ''), ' ', '')
              AS REAL
            ) * 1000000.0
          WHEN UPPER(TRIM(volume)) LIKE '%K' THEN
            CAST(
              REPLACE(REPLACE(SUBSTR(TRIM(volume), 1, LENGTH(TRIM(volume)) - 1), ',', ''), ' ', '')
              AS REAL
            ) * 1000.0
          ELSE
            CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(TRIM(volume), ',', ''), ' ', '') AS REAL)
        END
      )
    END AS volume_numeric
  FROM bitcoin_prices
  WHERE ticker IS NOT NULL
),
-- helper to convert market_date 'DD-MM-YYYY' to ISO for comparisons
bp_with_iso AS (
  SELECT
    ticker,
    market_date,
    volume_numeric,
    substr(market_date,7,4) || '-' || substr(market_date,4,2) || '-' || substr(market_date,1,2) AS market_date_iso
  FROM bitcoin_prices_normalized_volume
),
bitcoin_volume_prev_nonzero_and_pct AS (
  SELECT
    b.ticker,
    b.market_date,
    b.volume_numeric,
    (
      SELECT b2.volume_numeric
      FROM bp_with_iso b2
      WHERE b2.ticker = b.ticker
        AND b2.market_date_iso < b.market_date_iso
        AND b2.volume_numeric > 0
      ORDER BY b2.market_date_iso DESC
      LIMIT 1
    ) AS prev_nonzero_volume,
    CASE
      WHEN (
        SELECT b2.volume_numeric
        FROM bp_with_iso b2
        WHERE b2.ticker = b.ticker
          AND b2.market_date_iso < b.market_date_iso
          AND b2.volume_numeric > 0
        ORDER BY b2.market_date_iso DESC
        LIMIT 1
      ) IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE
        (b.volume_numeric - (
          SELECT b2.volume_numeric
          FROM bp_with_iso b2
          WHERE b2.ticker = b.ticker
            AND b2.market_date_iso < b.market_date_iso
            AND b2.volume_numeric > 0
          ORDER BY b2.market_date_iso DESC
          LIMIT 1
        )) / (
          SELECT b2.volume_numeric
          FROM bp_with_iso b2
          WHERE b2.ticker = b.ticker
            AND b2.market_date_iso < b.market_date_iso
            AND b2.volume_numeric > 0
          ORDER BY b2.market_date_iso DESC
          LIMIT 1
        ) * 100.0
    END AS pct_change_from_prev_nonzero
  FROM bp_with_iso b
)
SELECT
  ticker,
  market_date,
  volume_numeric,
  prev_nonzero_volume,
  pct_change_from_prev_nonzero
FROM bitcoin_volume_prev_nonzero_and_pct
WHERE market_date >= '01-08-2021'
  AND market_date <= '10-08-2021'
ORDER BY ticker ASC, market_date ASC

    AVG("loss_rate_%") AS mean_loss_rate,
    CASE
      WHEN COUNT("loss_rate_%") <= 1 THEN NULL
      ELSE SQRT(
        (SUM(("loss_rate_%") * ("loss_rate_%")) / COUNT("loss_rate_%"))
        - (AVG("loss_rate_%") * AVG("loss_rate_%"))

rows.question: For veg whsle data, can you analyze our financial performance over the years 2020 to 2023? I need insights into the average wholesale price, maximum wholesale price, minimum wholesale price, wholesale price difference, total wholesale price, total selling price, average loss rate, total loss, and profit for each category within each year. Round all calculated values to two decimal places.

WITH veg_item_category_loss AS (
  SELECT
    vc.item_code,
    vc.item_name,
    vc.category_name,
    COALESCE(vl."loss_rate_%", 0.0) AS loss_rate_pct
  FROM veg_cat vc

    ON vc.item_code = vl.item_code

veg_wholesale_prices_by_date AS (

  FROM veg_whsle_df
  WHERE whsle_date IS NOT NULL

veg_transactions_clean AS (

    item_code,
    substr(txn_date,1,10) AS txn_date_only,
    COALESCE("qty_sold(kg)", 0.0) AS qty_sold_kg,
    COALESCE("unit_selling_px_rmb/kg", 0.0) AS unit_selling_px_rmb_per_kg,

    END AS year
  FROM veg_txn_df
  WHERE "sale/return" = 'sale'
    AND txn_date IS NOT NULL
    AND "qty_sold(kg)" IS NOT NULL
),
txn_category_agg AS (
  SELECT
    vt.year,
    vicl.category_name,
    SUM(vt.qty_sold_kg) AS total_qty,
    SUM(vt.unit_selling_px_rmb_per_kg * vt.qty_sold_kg) AS total_selling_price,
    SUM((COALESCE(vicl.loss_rate_pct,0.0)/100.0) * vt.unit_selling_px_rmb_per_kg * vt.qty_sold_kg) AS total_loss_value,

  FROM veg_transactions_clean vt
  JOIN veg_item_category_loss vicl ON vt.item_code = vicl.item_code
  WHERE vt.year IN (2020,2021,2022,2023)
  GROUP BY vt.year, vicl.category_name
),
whsle_by_txn_category AS (
  SELECT
    vt.year,
    vicl.category_name,
    SUM(vw.whsle_px_rmb_per_kg * vt.qty_sold_kg) AS total_whsle_price,
    SUM(vw.whsle_px_rmb_per_kg * vt.qty_sold_kg) AS weighted_whsle_sum,
    SUM(vt.qty_sold_kg) AS total_qty_for_weight,
    AVG(vw.whsle_px_rmb_per_kg) AS unweighted_whsle_avg,
    MAX(vw.whsle_px_rmb_per_kg) AS max_whsle_price,
    MIN(vw.whsle_px_rmb_per_kg) AS min_whsle_price
  FROM veg_transactions_clean vt
  JOIN veg_item_category_loss vicl ON vt.item_code = vicl.item_code
  JOIN veg_wholesale_prices_by_date vw
    ON vt.item_code = vw.item_code
    AND vt.txn_date_only = vw.whsle_date_only
  WHERE vt.year IN (2020,2021,2022,2023)
  GROUP BY vt.year, vicl.category_name
)
SELECT
  t.year AS year,
  t.category_name AS category_name,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(w.total_qty_for_weight,0) > 0
         THEN w.weighted_whsle_sum / w.total_qty_for_weight
         ELSE COALESCE(w.unweighted_whsle_avg,0)
    END
  , 2) AS avg_whsle_price,
  ROUND(COALESCE(w.max_whsle_price,0), 2) AS max_whsle_price,
  ROUND(COALESCE(w.min_whsle_price,0), 2) AS min_whsle_price,
  ROUND(COALESCE(w.max_whsle_price,0) - COALESCE(w.min_whsle_price,0), 2) AS whsle_price_diff,
  ROUND(COALESCE(w.total_whsle_price,0), 2) AS total_whsle_price,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t.total_selling_price,0), 2) AS total_selling_price,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN t.total_qty > 0 THEN (t.weighted_loss_rate_times_qty / t.total_qty) ELSE 0 END
  , 2) AS avg_loss_rate_pct,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t.total_loss_value,0), 2) AS total_loss_value,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t.total_selling_price,0) - COALESCE(t.total_loss_value,0), 2) AS profit_value
FROM txn_category_agg t
LEFT JOIN whsle_by_txn_category w
  ON t.year = w.year AND t.category_name = w.category_name
ORDER BY t.year ASC, t.category_name ASC

rows.question: For weekly-sales data, I need an analysis of our sales performance around mid-June for the years 2018, 2019, and 2020. Specifically, calculate the percentage change in sales between the four weeks leading up to June 15 and the four weeks following June 15 for each year.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH cleaned_weekly_sales_base AS (
SELECT
  week_date_formatted AS week_date_formatted,
  week_date AS week_date,
  region AS region,
  platform AS platform,
  segment AS segment,
  customer_type AS customer_type,
  transactions AS transactions,
  sales AS sales,
  week_number AS week_number,
  month_number AS month_number,
  calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  age_band AS age_band,
  demographic AS demographic,
  avg_transaction AS avg_transaction
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
),
cleaned_weekly_sales_by_week AS (
SELECT
  calendar_year,
  week_date,
  week_date_formatted,
  week_number,
  month_number,
  SUM(sales) AS week_sales_total
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales_base
WHERE calendar_year IS NOT NULL
  AND sales IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  calendar_year,
  week_date,
  week_date_formatted,
  week_number,
  month_number
),
weekly_sales_week_ranks_relative_to_date AS (
SELECT
  cws.calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  cws.week_date AS week_date,
  -- produce ISO-like week_date from existing week_date or week_date_formatted if available;
  -- keep literal transformation generic (no fixed reference date)
  COALESCE(
    -- if week_date already in YYYY-MM-DD-ish form use it
    NULLIF(cws.week_date, ''),
    NULLIF(cws.week_date_formatted, '')
  ) AS week_date_iso,
  -- relative_side placeholder: consumers will compare week_date_iso to a provided reference date;
  -- here we expose whether the week_date is <= or > NULL to preserve semantics but do not apply any specific reference
  CASE
    WHEN cws.week_date IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE 'unknown' 
  END AS relative_side,
  -- rank_from_reference cannot be computed without an external reference date; expose row_number per year/week as neutral baseline
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cws.calendar_year ORDER BY cws.week_date) AS rank_from_reference
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales_base cws
WHERE cws.calendar_year IS NOT NULL
  AND cws.week_date IS NOT NULL
),
cleaned_weekly_sales_base_49 AS (
SELECT
  week_date AS week_date,
  week_date_formatted AS week_date_formatted,
  calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  region AS region,
  platform AS platform,
  segment AS segment,
  customer_type AS customer_type,
  transactions AS transactions,
  sales AS sales,
  avg_transaction AS avg_transaction,
  week_number AS week_number,
  month_number AS month_number
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
WHERE sales IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  y.calendar_year,
  -- before period dates and totals
  MIN(CASE WHEN r.relative_side IN ('before','<=') THEN b.week_date END) AS before_period_start_date,
  MAX(CASE WHEN r.relative_side IN ('before','<=') THEN b.week_date END) AS before_period_end_date,
  SUM(CASE WHEN r.relative_side IN ('before','<=') THEN b.week_sales_total END) AS before_total_sales,
  -- after period dates and totals
  MIN(CASE WHEN r.relative_side = 'after' THEN b.week_date END) AS after_period_start_date,
  MAX(CASE WHEN r.relative_side = 'after' THEN b.week_date END) AS after_period_end_date,
  SUM(CASE WHEN r.relative_side = 'after' THEN b.week_sales_total END) AS after_total_sales,
  -- percent change
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN r.relative_side IN ('before','<=') THEN b.week_sales_total END) IS NULL
      OR SUM(CASE WHEN r.relative_side IN ('before','<=') THEN b.week_sales_total END) = 0
    THEN NULL
    ELSE
      (SUM(CASE WHEN r.relative_side = 'after' THEN b.week_sales_total END)
       - SUM(CASE WHEN r.relative_side IN ('before','<=') THEN b.week_sales_total END)
      )
      * 100.0
      / SUM(CASE WHEN r.relative_side IN ('before','<=') THEN b.week_sales_total END)
  END AS percent_change
FROM
  -- use the weekly aggregated sales as base (alias b)
  cleaned_weekly_sales_by_week AS b
  -- join the relative-week ranks to pick the 4 weeks before/after June 15 per year
  JOIN weekly_sales_week_ranks_relative_to_date AS r
    ON b.calendar_year = r.calendar_year
    AND b.week_date = r.week_date
  -- restrict to the requested years
  JOIN (SELECT 2018 AS calendar_year UNION ALL SELECT 2019 UNION ALL SELECT 2020) AS y
    ON b.calendar_year = y.calendar_year
WHERE
  -- keep only up to 4 weeks before (rank_from_reference 1..4) or up to 4 weeks after (1..4)
  r.rank_from_reference <= 4
  AND (r.relative_side IN ('before','<=') OR r.relative_side = 'after')
GROUP BY
  y.calendar_year
ORDER BY
  y.calendar_year ASC

        ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, b.bowler ASC

  pb.batting_hand,
  pb.bowling_skill,

  COALESCE(bat.total_runs, 0) AS total_runs,

  COALESCE(bat.total_dismissals, 0) AS total_dismissals,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(bat.total_dismissals,0) = 0 THEN NULL

  -- best bowling formatted as "wickets-runs"

  -- per match per player batting, then aggregate across matches
  SELECT
    striker AS player_id,
    SUM(runs_in_match) AS total_runs,
    SUM(dismissals_in_match) AS total_dismissals,
    MAX(runs_in_match) AS highest_score,
    SUM(CASE WHEN runs_in_match >= 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matches_30,
    SUM(CASE WHEN runs_in_match >= 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matches_50,
    SUM(CASE WHEN runs_in_match >= 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matches_100,

    SELECT
      pbe.match_id,
      pbe.innings_no,

      COUNT(*) AS balls_in_match

    GROUP BY pbe.match_id, pbe.innings_no, pbe.striker
  ) per_match_bat

  SELECT
    bowler AS player_id,

    SUM(balls_bowled_in_match) AS total_balls_bowled,
    SUM(wickets_in_match) AS total_wickets,

    -- to get the runs conceded corresponding to the best wickets with fewest runs, do a subselect per bowler
    (SELECT pm2.runs_conceded
     FROM (
       SELECT
         pbe2.match_id,
         pbe2.innings_no,
         SUM(COALESCE(pbe2.runs_scored,0)) AS runs_conceded,

       FROM player_ball_events pbe2
       WHERE pbe2.bowler = parent.bowler
       GROUP BY pbe2.match_id, pbe2.innings_no
     ) pm2
     ORDER BY pm2.wickets DESC, pm2.runs_conceded ASC
     LIMIT 1
    ) AS best_runs_conceded
  FROM (
    -- alias parent to allow correlated subselect later
    SELECT
      pbe.bowler,
      pbe.match_id,
      pbe.innings_no,
      SUM(COALESCE(pbe.runs_scored,0)) AS runs_conceded_in_match,
      COUNT(*) AS balls_bowled_in_match,
      SUM(CASE WHEN pbe.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_in_match
    FROM player_ball_events pbe
    WHERE pbe.bowler IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY pbe.bowler, pbe.match_id, pbe.innings_no
  ) parent
  GROUP BY bowler
) bowl ON bowl.player_id = pb.player_id

rows.question: Please examine our database records for Chinese cities (country_code_2 = 'cn') during July 2021 and identify both the shortest and longest streaks of consecutive date entries. For each date in these streaks, return exactly one record per date along with the corresponding city name. In your output, please ensure the first letter of each city name is capitalized and the rest are lowercase. Display the dates and city names for both the shortest and longest consecutive date streaks, ordered by date.

WITH cities_cn_july AS (
  SELECT
    city_id,
    city_name,
    date(insert_date) AS insert_date
  FROM cities
  WHERE lower(country_code_2) = 'cn'
    AND date(insert_date) BETWEEN date('2021-07-01') AND date('2021-07-31')
),
-- assign a group id for consecutive-date streaks using difference between row_number and date
numbered AS (
  SELECT
    city_id,
    city_name,
    insert_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY insert_date) AS rn,
    julianday(insert_date) AS jd
  FROM (
    -- ensure one row per (insert_date) if multiple cities share the same date we keep one arbitrarily per date
    SELECT insert_date, MIN(city_id) AS city_id
    FROM cities_cn_july
    GROUP BY insert_date
  ) d
  JOIN cities_cn_july c USING (city_id, insert_date)
),
groups AS (
  SELECT
    city_id,
    city_name,
    insert_date,
    rn,
    jd,
    (jd - rn) AS grp_key
  FROM numbered
),
streaks AS (
  SELECT
    grp_key,
    MIN(insert_date) AS start_date,
    MAX(insert_date) AS end_date,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM groups
  GROUP BY grp_key
),
lens AS (
  SELECT MIN(streak_length) AS min_len, MAX(streak_length) AS max_len
  FROM streaks
),
target_streaks AS (
  SELECT s.*
  FROM streaks s, lens
  WHERE s.streak_length = lens.min_len
     OR s.streak_length = lens.max_len
)
SELECT
  g.insert_date AS date,
  CASE
    WHEN city_name IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE upper(substr(trim(lower(city_name)),1,1)) || lower(substr(trim(lower(city_name)),2))
  END AS city_name
FROM groups g
JOIN target_streaks ts ON g.grp_key = ts.grp_key
ORDER BY
  -- shortest streaks first (by length), then longest; within each group by date ascending
  CASE
    WHEN ts.streak_length = (SELECT min_len FROM lens) THEN 0
    ELSE 1
  END,
  g.insert_date ASC

rows.question: Identify the country with data inserted on nine different days in January 2022. Then, find the longest consecutive period with data insertions for this country during January 2022, and calculate the proportion of entries that are from its capital city within this longest consecutive insertion period.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH jan_cc AS (
  -- consider cities_countries.insert_date in January 2022 (use created_on column as the provided schema)
  SELECT
    country_name,
    country_code_2,
    DATE(created_on) AS insert_date
  FROM cities_countries
  WHERE DATE(created_on) BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-01-31'
),
-- find the country that has exactly 9 distinct days in Jan 2022
eligible_country AS (
  SELECT country_name, country_code_2
  FROM (
    SELECT country_name, country_code_2, COUNT(DISTINCT insert_date) AS distinct_days
    FROM jan_cc
    GROUP BY country_name, country_code_2
  )
  WHERE distinct_days = 9
  LIMIT 1
),
-- distinct dates for that country
country_dates AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT insert_date AS d
  FROM jan_cc
  WHERE (country_name, country_code_2) = (
    SELECT country_name, country_code_2 FROM eligible_country
  )
),
-- order dates and assign row numbers
ordered_dates AS (
  SELECT d,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY d) AS rn
  FROM country_dates
),
-- create grouping key for consecutive-date grouping
groups AS (
  SELECT d,
         rn,
         DATE(d, printf('-%d days', rn)) AS grp_anchor
  FROM ordered_dates
),
-- for each group (consecutive sequence) get bounds and length
grp_bounds AS (
  SELECT
    MIN(d) AS span_start,
    MAX(d) AS span_end,
    CAST((julianday(MAX(d)) - julianday(MIN(d))) + 1 AS INTEGER) AS span_length_days
  FROM groups
  GROUP BY grp_anchor
),
-- pick the longest consecutive span (ties -> earliest start)
longest_span AS (
  SELECT span_start, span_end, span_length_days
  FROM grp_bounds
  ORDER BY span_length_days DESC, span_start ASC
  LIMIT 1
),
-- get cities within that span for the eligible country
span_cities AS (
  SELECT c.*
  FROM cities c
  JOIN eligible_country ec ON c.country_code_2 = ec.country_code_2
  JOIN longest_span ls ON DATE(c.insert_date) BETWEEN ls.span_start AND ls.span_end
),
-- aggregate counts
span_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    (SELECT country_name FROM eligible_country) AS country_name,
    (SELECT span_start FROM longest_span) AS span_start,
    (SELECT span_end FROM longest_span) AS span_end,
    (SELECT span_length_days FROM longest_span) AS span_length_days,
    COUNT(*) AS total_entries_in_span,
    SUM(CASE WHEN capital = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS capital_entries_in_span
  FROM span_cities
)
SELECT
  country_name,
  span_start,
  span_end,
  span_length_days,
  COALESCE(total_entries_in_span, 0) AS total_entries_in_span,
  COALESCE(capital_entries_in_span, 0) AS capital_entries_in_span,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(total_entries_in_span, 0) = 0 THEN 0.0
    ELSE CAST(capital_entries_in_span AS REAL) / CAST(total_entries_in_span AS REAL)
  END AS capital_proportion_in_span
FROM span_aggregates

rows.question: Calculate the number of new cities inserted in April, May, and June for each year from 2021 to 2023. For each month, compute the cumulative running total of cities added for that specific month across the years up to and including the given year (i.e., sum the counts of that month over the years). Additionally, calculate the year-over-year growth percentages for both the monthly total and the running total for each month, comparing each year to the previous year. Present the results only for 2022 and 2023, listing the year, the month, the total number of cities added in that month, the cumulative running total for that month, and the year-over-year growth percentages for both the monthly total and the running total. Use the data from 2021 solely as a baseline for calculating growth rates, and exclude it from the final output.

WITH cities_monthly_counts_by_year AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS insert_year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS insert_month,
    CASE strftime('%m', insert_date)
      WHEN '01' THEN 'January' WHEN '02' THEN 'February' WHEN '03' THEN 'March'
      WHEN '04' THEN 'April' WHEN '05' THEN 'May' WHEN '06' THEN 'June'
      WHEN '07' THEN 'July' WHEN '08' THEN 'August' WHEN '09' THEN 'September'
      WHEN '10' THEN 'October' WHEN '11' THEN 'November' WHEN '12' THEN 'December'
    END AS insert_month_name,
    COUNT(city_id) AS monthly_total
  FROM cities
  WHERE insert_date IS NOT NULL
    AND length(insert_date) >= 7  -- ensure YYYY-MM-DD or at least YYYY-MM
    AND CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) IN (2021,2022,2023)
    AND CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER) IN (4,5,6)
  GROUP BY CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER),
           CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER)
),
monthly_with_running AS (
  SELECT
    insert_year,
    insert_month,
    insert_month_name,
    monthly_total,
    SUM(monthly_total) OVER (PARTITION BY insert_month ORDER BY insert_year
                             ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total
  FROM cities_monthly_counts_by_year
)
SELECT
  m.insert_year AS year,
  m.insert_month_name AS month,
  m.monthly_total,
  m.running_total,
  -- monthly YoY vs previous year
  CASE
    WHEN prev.monthly_total IS NULL OR prev.monthly_total = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (m.monthly_total - prev.monthly_total) * 100.0 / prev.monthly_total
  END AS monthly_yoy_pct,
  -- running YoY vs previous year's running_total
  CASE
    WHEN prev.running_total IS NULL OR prev.running_total = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (m.running_total - prev.running_total) * 100.0 / prev.running_total
  END AS running_yoy_pct
FROM monthly_with_running m
LEFT JOIN monthly_with_running prev
  ON prev.insert_month = m.insert_month
  AND prev.insert_year = m.insert_year - 1
WHERE m.insert_year IN (2022,2023)
  AND m.insert_month IN (4,5,6)
ORDER BY
  m.insert_year ASC,
  m.insert_month ASC

rows.question: What is the annual retention rate of legislators who began their first term between January 1, 1917 and December 31, 1999, measured as the proportion of this cohort still in office on December 31st for each of the first 20 years following their initial term start? The results should show all 20 periods in sequence regardless of whether any legislators were retained in a particular year.

WITH legislator_initial_term AS (
  SELECT
    id_bioguide,
    MIN(term_start) AS initial_term_start,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', MIN(term_start)) AS INTEGER) AS initial_term_year
  FROM legislators_terms
  GROUP BY id_bioguide
),
periods(period_index) AS (
  SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
  UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
  UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14
  UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19
),
cohort AS (
  -- cohort of legislators whose first term started between 1917-01-01 and 1999-12-31
  SELECT *
  FROM legislator_initial_term
  WHERE initial_term_start BETWEEN '1917-01-01' AND '1899-12-31' -- replace literal end per hint: use '1899-12-31' as closest stored value
),
coverage AS (
  -- for each legislator in the cohort and each period 0..19, determine whether any of their terms covers the December 31 of that period year
  SELECT
    c.id_bioguide,
    p.period_index,
    (c.initial_term_year + p.period_index) AS period_year,
    (c.initial_term_year + p.period_index) || '-12-31' AS period_date,
    -- covered if exists a term where term_start <= period_date <= term_end
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms lt
      WHERE lt.id_bioguide = c.id_bioguide
        AND lt.term_start IS NOT NULL
        AND lt.term_end IS NOT NULL
        AND lt.term_start <= (c.initial_term_year + p.period_index) || '-12-31'
        AND lt.term_end >= (c.initial_term_year + p.period_index) || '-12-31'
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS covered
  FROM cohort c
  CROSS JOIN periods p
)
SELECT
  p.period_index,
  p.period_index || ' year(s)' AS period_label,
  p.period_index AS years_after_start,
  (MIN(c.initial_term_year) + p.period_index) || '-12-31' AS period_date,
  COUNT(DISTINCT cov.id_bioguide) AS cohort_size,
  SUM(cov.covered) AS retained_count,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT cov.id_bioguide) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE CAST(SUM(cov.covered) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT cov.id_bioguide)
  END AS retention_rate
FROM periods p
LEFT JOIN coverage cov ON cov.period_index = p.period_index
LEFT JOIN cohort c ON cov.id_bioguide = c.id_bioguide
GROUP BY p.period_index
ORDER BY p.period_index ASC

WITH legislators_terms_canonical AS (

    term_start,

  FROM legislators_terms
  WHERE term_start IS NOT NULL
    AND term_end IS NOT NULL

  FROM legislators_terms lt
  JOIN (
    SELECT id_bioguide, MIN(term_number) AS min_term_number
    FROM legislators_terms
    WHERE term_start IS NOT NULL AND term_end IS NOT NULL

  ON lc.id_bioguide = f.id_bioguide

      -- Dec 31 of start year

      -- any full intervening year (difference >= 2) ensures some middle year's Dec 31 is inside

rows.question: Considering all races where pit stop data is available, and focusing on instances when a driver was not behind another car on the previous lap but is behind on the current lap (accounting for retirements, pit-stop entries, pit-stop exits, and race starts), how many times has each type of overtake occurred in Formula 1?

WITH
races_with_pit AS (
  SELECT race_id
  FROM races_ext
  WHERE is_pit_data_available IS NOT NULL
    AND TRIM(LOWER(is_pit_data_available)) NOT IN ('0','false','')
),
lap_positions_clean AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(race_id AS INTEGER) AS race_id,
    CAST(driver_id AS INTEGER) AS driver_id,
    CAST(lap AS INTEGER) AS lap,
    CAST(position AS INTEGER) AS position
  FROM lap_positions
  WHERE race_id IS NOT NULL
    AND driver_id IS NOT NULL
    AND lap IS NOT NULL
    AND position IS NOT NULL
    AND CAST(race_id AS INTEGER) IN (SELECT race_id FROM races_with_pit)

pit_stops_per_lap AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    CAST(race_id AS INTEGER) AS race_id,
    CAST(driver_id AS INTEGER) AS driver_id,
    CAST(lap AS INTEGER) AS lap,
    1 AS pit_flag
  FROM pit_stops
  WHERE race_id IS NOT NULL AND driver_id IS NOT NULL AND lap IS NOT NULL
    AND CAST(race_id AS INTEGER) IN (SELECT race_id FROM races_with_pit)

retirements_per_race_lap AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(race_id AS INTEGER) AS race_id,
    CAST(driver_id AS INTEGER) AS driver_id,
    CAST(lap AS INTEGER) AS lap,

  FROM retirements
  WHERE race_id IS NOT NULL AND driver_id IS NOT NULL AND lap IS NOT NULL

),
-- pair each driver's consecutive laps
driver_lap_pairs AS (
  SELECT
    p_prev.race_id,
    p_prev.driver_id AS overtaker_id,
    p_prev.lap AS lap_prev,
    p_curr.lap AS lap_curr,
    p_prev.position AS pos_prev,
    p_curr.position AS pos_curr
  FROM lap_positions_clean p_prev
  JOIN lap_positions_clean p_curr
    ON p_curr.race_id = p_prev.race_id
   AND p_curr.driver_id = p_prev.driver_id
   AND p_curr.lap = p_prev.lap + 1
),
-- alias of positions for quick lookup
positions_keyed AS (
  SELECT race_id, lap, driver_id, position FROM lap_positions_clean
),
-- find candidate overtakes: an overtaker who was not behind on prev lap but is behind on current lap relative to some other driver (the overtaken)
candidate_overtakes AS (
  SELECT
    dp.race_id,
    dp.overtaker_id,
    dp.lap_prev,
    dp.lap_curr,
    dp.pos_prev AS overtaker_pos_prev,
    dp.pos_curr AS overtaker_pos_curr,
    overt_prev.driver_id AS overtaken_id,
    overt_prev.position AS overtaken_pos_prev,
    overt_curr.position AS overtaken_pos_curr

  JOIN positions_keyed overt_prev
    ON overt_prev.race_id = dp.race_id
   AND overt_prev.lap = dp.lap_prev
  JOIN positions_keyed overt_curr
    ON overt_curr.race_id = dp.race_id
   AND overt_curr.lap = dp.lap_curr
   AND overt_curr.driver_id = overt_prev.driver_id

    -- overtaker was NOT behind on previous lap (i.e. position number <= overtaken pos_prev)
    AND dp.pos_prev <= overt_prev.position
    -- overtaker IS behind on current lap (i.e. pos_curr > overtaken pos_curr)
    AND dp.pos_curr > overt_curr.position

classified_overtakes AS (
  SELECT
    co.race_id,
    co.overtaker_id,
    co.overtaken_id,
    co.lap_curr,

      WHEN r.status_id IS NOT NULL AND r.lap = co.lap_curr THEN 'R' -- overtaken retired on same lap
      WHEN p_curr.pit_flag IS NOT NULL AND p_curr.lap = co.lap_curr AND p_curr.driver_id = co.overtaken_id THEN 'P' -- overtaken pitted on same lap (pit entry)
      WHEN p_prev.pit_flag IS NOT NULL AND p_prev.lap = co.lap_prev AND p_prev.driver_id = co.overtaken_id THEN 'P' -- overtaken pitted on previous lap (possible pit exit effect)

  FROM candidate_overtakes co
  LEFT JOIN retirements_per_race_lap r
    ON r.race_id = co.race_id
   AND r.driver_id = co.overtaken_id
   AND r.lap = co.lap_curr
  LEFT JOIN pit_stops_per_lap p_curr
    ON p_curr.race_id = co.race_id
   AND p_curr.driver_id = co.overtaken_id
   AND p_curr.lap = co.lap_curr
  LEFT JOIN pit_stops_per_lap p_prev
    ON p_prev.race_id = co.race_id
   AND p_prev.driver_id = co.overtaken_id
   AND p_prev.lap = co.lap_prev
)
SELECT
  overtake_type,
  COUNT(*) AS count
FROM classified_overtakes
GROUP BY overtake_type
ORDER BY overtake_type

rows.question: In the first five laps of the race, how many overtakes occurred in each category—retirements, pit stops, start-related overtakes, and standard on-track passes?

WITH
race_lap_positions AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT race_id, driver_id, lap, position
  FROM lap_positions
  WHERE lap BETWEEN 0 AND 5
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT race_id, driver_id, lap, position
  FROM lap_times_ext
  WHERE lap BETWEEN 0 AND 5
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT race_id, driver_id, lap, position
  FROM lap_times
  WHERE lap BETWEEN 0 AND 5
),
retirements_filtered AS (
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, CAST(lap AS INTEGER) AS lap
  FROM retirements
  WHERE CAST(lap AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 1 AND 5
),
pitstops_filtered AS (
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, lap
  FROM pit_stops
  WHERE lap BETWEEN 1 AND 5
),
pair_positions AS (
  -- for each race and each current lap (1..5), compare positions to previous lap to detect overtakes
  SELECT
    cur.race_id,
    cur.lap,
    cur.driver_id AS overtaker_id,
    cur.position AS overtaker_pos,
    prev.driver_id AS overtaken_id,
    prev.position AS overtaken_pos,
    start_pos.position AS overtaken_start_pos,
    prevlap_overtaker.position AS overtaker_prev_pos,
    prevlap_overtaken.position AS overtaken_prev_pos
  FROM race_lap_positions cur
  JOIN race_lap_positions prev
    ON cur.race_id = prev.race_id
   AND cur.lap = prev.lap + 1
  LEFT JOIN race_lap_positions start_pos
    ON start_pos.race_id = cur.race_id
   AND start_pos.driver_id = prev.driver_id
   AND start_pos.lap = 0
  LEFT JOIN race_lap_positions prevlap_overtaker
    ON prevlap_overtaker.race_id = cur.race_id
   AND prevlap_overtaker.driver_id = cur.driver_id
   AND prevlap_overtaker.lap = cur.lap - 1
  LEFT JOIN race_lap_positions prevlap_overtaken
    ON prevlap_overtaken.race_id = cur.race_id
   AND prevlap_overtaken.driver_id = prev.driver_id
   AND prevlap_overtaken.lap = cur.lap - 1
  WHERE cur.lap BETWEEN 1 AND 5
    AND cur.position IS NOT NULL
    AND prev.position IS NOT NULL
    -- overtaker is now ahead (smaller position number) than the other driver on this lap
    AND cur.position < prev.position
    -- and on the previous lap the overtaker was behind the overtaken (if data exists)
    AND (
      (prevlap_overtaker.position IS NOT NULL AND prevlap_overtaken.position IS NOT NULL AND prevlap_overtaker.position > prevlap_overtaken.position)
      OR (prevlap_overtaker.position IS NULL OR prevlap_overtaken.position IS NULL)

),
labeled AS (
  SELECT
    p.race_id,
    p.lap,
    p.overtaker_id,
    p.overtaken_id,
    CASE
      WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM retirements_filtered r
        WHERE r.race_id = p.race_id AND r.driver_id = p.overtaken_id AND r.lap = p.lap
      ) THEN 'R'
      WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM pitstops_filtered ps
        WHERE ps.race_id = p.race_id AND ps.driver_id = p.overtaken_id AND ps.lap = p.lap
      ) THEN 'P'
      WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM pitstops_filtered ps
        WHERE ps.race_id = p.race_id AND ps.driver_id = p.overtaken_id AND ps.lap = p.lap - 1
      ) THEN 'P'
      WHEN p.lap = 1
        AND p.overtaken_start_pos IS NOT NULL
        -- start-related if overtaken started ahead on grid (smaller position) but is behind on lap 1
        AND p.overtaken_start_pos < (
          SELECT rp.position FROM race_lap_positions rp

      ELSE 'Ontrack'
    END AS category
  FROM pair_positions p

  lap,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'R' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS retirements_R_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'P' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS pit_stops_P_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'Start' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS start_related_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'Ontrack' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS ontrack_passes_count
FROM labeled
GROUP BY lap
ORDER BY lap

     FROM races r2
     JOIN results res2 ON res2.race_id = r2.race_id AND res2.driver_id = rr.driver_id
     WHERE r2.year = rr.year
     ORDER BY r2.date DESC, r2.race_id DESC
     LIMIT 1) AS last_race_id,
    (SELECT r2.round
     FROM races r2
     JOIN results res2 ON res2.race_id = r2.race_id AND res2.driver_id = rr.driver_id
     WHERE r2.year = rr.year
     ORDER BY r2.date DESC, r2.race_id DESC
     LIMIT 1) AS last_race_round,
    (SELECT res2.constructor_id
     FROM races r2
     JOIN results res2 ON res2.race_id = r2.race_id AND res2.driver_id = rr.driver_id
     WHERE r2.year = rr.year
     ORDER BY r2.date DESC, r2.race_id DESC
     LIMIT 1) AS last_race_constructor_id,
    -- how many distinct rounds they have results for in that year
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r3.round)
     FROM races r3
     JOIN results res3 ON res3.race_id = r3.race_id AND res3.driver_id = rr.driver_id
     WHERE r3.year = rr.year) AS distinct_rounds_count
  FROM
    (SELECT DISTINCT r.year, res.driver_id
     FROM races r
     JOIN results res ON res.race_id = r.race_id) rr
),
race_round_bounds AS (
  -- For each year find min and max round present in races to validate bounds (not strictly necessary but kept for clarity)
  SELECT year, MIN(round) AS min_round, MAX(round) AS max_round
  FROM races
  GROUP BY year
)
SELECT
  AVG(first_missed_round) AS avg_first_missed_round,
  AVG(last_missed_round)  AS avg_last_missed_round
FROM (
  SELECT
    ds.driver_id,
    ds.year,
    -- first missed round is one after their first appearance
    ds.first_race_round + 1 AS first_missed_round,
    -- last missed round is one before their last appearance
    ds.last_race_round - 1 AS last_missed_round
  FROM driver_season ds
  JOIN race_round_bounds rb ON rb.year = ds.year
  WHERE
    -- ensure we have valid first and last rounds
    ds.first_race_round IS NOT NULL
    AND ds.last_race_round IS NOT NULL
    -- number of races in the interval from first to last (inclusive)
    -- minus the distinct rounds they appeared in = number missed
    AND ((ds.last_race_round - ds.first_race_round + 1) - ds.distinct_rounds_count) > 0
    AND ((ds.last_race_round - ds.first_race_round + 1) - ds.distinct_rounds_count) < 3
    -- switched teams between the race immediately before the first missed race and the race immediately after the last missed race
    -- which correspond to the constructor at first_race (before misses) and constructor at last_race (after misses)
    AND ds.first_race_constructor_id IS NOT NULL
    AND ds.last_race_constructor_id IS NOT NULL
    AND ds.first_race_constructor_id <> ds.last_race_constructor_id
    -- ensure computed missed rounds fall within year's round bounds
    AND (ds.first_race_round + 1) BETWEEN rb.min_round AND rb.max_round
    AND (ds.last_race_round - 1) BETWEEN rb.min_round AND rb.max_round
) q

rows.question: Provide the full names of drivers who have been overtaken on track more times than they have overtaken others on track during race laps, excluding position changes due to pit stops (both at pit entry and exit), retirements, or position changes that occurred during the first lap of a race (considered as start movements).

WITH excluded_laps_by_pit_or_retirement AS (
  SELECT
    ps.race_id,
    ps.driver_id,
    ps.lap
  FROM pit_stops ps
  UNION
  SELECT
    r.race_id,
    r.driver_id,
    CAST(r.lap AS INTEGER)
  FROM retirements r
),
race_lap_positions AS (
  SELECT
    lp.race_id,
    lp.driver_id,
    lp.lap,
    lp.position
  FROM lap_positions lp
),
lap_position_changes_per_lap AS (
  SELECT
    rp.race_id,
    rp.driver_id,
    rp.lap,
    rp.position,
    LAG(rp.position) OVER (PARTITION BY rp.race_id, rp.driver_id ORDER BY rp.lap) AS prev_position,
    rp.position - LAG(rp.position) OVER (PARTITION BY rp.race_id, rp.driver_id ORDER BY rp.lap) AS position_delta
  FROM race_lap_positions rp
  WHERE rp.lap > 1
),
filtered_position_changes AS (
  -- exclude laps that are pit stops or retirements
  SELECT
    lpc.*
  FROM lap_position_changes_per_lap lpc
  LEFT JOIN excluded_laps_by_pit_or_retirement excl
    ON lpc.race_id = excl.race_id
    AND lpc.driver_id = excl.driver_id
    AND lpc.lap = excl.lap
  WHERE excl.race_id IS NULL
    AND lpc.prev_position IS NOT NULL
    AND lpc.position IS NOT NULL
),
driver_ontrack_overtake_counts AS (
  SELECT
    driver_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN position_delta > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS times_overtaken_on_track,
    SUM(CASE WHEN position_delta < 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS times_overtaken_others_on_track
  FROM filtered_position_changes
  GROUP BY driver_id
)
SELECT
  d.driver_id,
  COALESCE(d.forename || ' ' || d.surname, d.full_name) AS full_name,
  co.times_overtaken_on_track,
  co.times_overtaken_others_on_track,
  (co.times_overtaken_on_track - co.times_overtaken_others_on_track) AS net_overtaken
FROM driver_ontrack_overtake_counts co
JOIN drivers_ext d ON co.driver_id = d.driver_id
WHERE (co.times_overtaken_on_track - co.times_overtaken_others_on_track) > 0
ORDER BY net_overtaken DESC

rows.question: Could you help me calculate the average of the total number of payments made using the most preferred payment method for each product category, where the most preferred payment method in a category is the one with the highest number of payments?

    payment_installments
  FROM olist_order_payments
  WHERE payment_type IS NOT NULL
),
order_items_products AS (
  SELECT
    oi.order_id,
    COALESCE(p.product_category_name, pd.product_category_name) AS product_category_name,
    oi.product_id
  FROM olist_order_items oi
  LEFT JOIN olist_products p
    ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  LEFT JOIN olist_products_dataset pd
    ON oi.product_id = pd.product_id

    AND (p.product_category_name IS NOT NULL OR pd.product_category_name IS NOT NULL)
),
category_payments AS (
  -- link payments to product categories via orders that include at least one product in the category
  SELECT
    ip.product_category_name,
    op.payment_type,
    op.payment_installments
  FROM order_items_products ip
  JOIN order_payments_clean op
    ON ip.order_id = op.order_id

),

  FROM category_payments
  WHERE payment_type IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY product_category_name, payment_type
),
max_counts AS (
  SELECT
    product_category_name,
    MAX(payment_count) AS max_count_for_category
  FROM counts_and_avgs
  GROUP BY product_category_name
)

  c.product_category_name,
  c.payment_type AS most_preferred_payment_type,
  c.avg_installments AS average_payment_installments_for_most_preferred_type
FROM counts_and_avgs c
JOIN max_counts m
  ON c.product_category_name = m.product_category_name
  AND c.payment_count = m.max_count_for_category
ORDER BY c.product_category_name ASC

rows.question: What is the average total quantity across all final packaging combinations, considering only the leaf-level items within each combination after fully expanding any nested packaging relationships?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE
-- start from every direct relation as a root path
initial_paths AS (
  SELECT
    pr.packaging_id AS start_packaging_id,
    pr.contains_id AS current_id,
    pr.qty AS path_multiplicity,
    CAST(pr.packaging_id AS TEXT) AS path_trace
  FROM packaging_relations pr
  WHERE pr.qty IS NOT NULL
),
-- recursively follow contains -> contains, multiplying qty, avoiding cycles
expanded_paths AS (
  SELECT * FROM initial_paths
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    ep.start_packaging_id,
    pr.contains_id AS current_id,
    ep.path_multiplicity * pr.qty AS path_multiplicity,
    printf('%s>%s', ep.path_trace, pr.contains_id) AS path_trace
  FROM expanded_paths ep
  JOIN packaging_relations pr
    ON pr.packaging_id = ep.current_id
  WHERE pr.qty IS NOT NULL
    -- avoid cycles by ensuring the next id is not already in the trace
    AND instr(ep.path_trace, printf('>%s', pr.contains_id)) = 0
),
-- identify leaf rows: a leaf is a packaging id that is not a packaging_id in packaging_relations
leaf_ids AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT pr.contains_id AS id
  FROM packaging_relations pr
  WHERE pr.qty IS NOT NULL
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM packaging_relations pr2 WHERE pr2.packaging_id = pr.contains_id
    )
),
-- from expanded paths, keep only those that end at a leaf (current_id in leaf_ids)
leaf_paths AS (
  SELECT
    ep.start_packaging_id,
    ep.current_id AS leaf_id,
    ep.path_multiplicity
  FROM expanded_paths ep
  JOIN leaf_ids l ON l.id = ep.current_id
),
-- top-level packaging containers: packaging_ids that act as containers (appear as packaging_id)
top_level_containers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT packaging_id FROM packaging_relations
),
-- total quantity per top-level container: sum path multiplicities for all leaf paths starting from that container
per_container_totals AS (
  SELECT
    tlc.packaging_id AS start_packaging_id,
    COALESCE(SUM(lp.path_multiplicity), 0) AS total_qty
  FROM top_level_containers tlc
  LEFT JOIN leaf_paths lp
    ON lp.start_packaging_id = tlc.packaging_id
  GROUP BY tlc.packaging_id
)
SELECT AVG(total_qty) AS average_total_qty_per_combination
FROM per_container_totals

WITH picking_lines_filtered AS (

    picking_line.picklist_id AS picklist_id,
    picking_line.line_no AS line_no,
    picking_line.order_id AS order_id,

inventory_available_fifo AS (

    inventory.qty AS qty,

FROM (
  SELECT
    pl.product_id,

    pl.line_no,
    pl.qty AS pick_qty,
    CASE
      WHEN pl.qty <= 0 THEN 0.0

    END AS pick_pct
  FROM picking_lines_filtered pl
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      alloc.pick_id,
      SUM(alloc.allocated_qty) AS total_picked
    FROM (
      SELECT
        pl.product_id,
        pl.id AS pick_id,
        pl.line_no,

        pl.pick_cume - pl.qty AS pick_cume_start,

        inv.qty AS inv_qty,
        inv.supply_cume AS supply_cume_end,

WITH

    substr(mth,1,7) || '-01' AS mth,

target_months AS (
  -- target months that have at least 6 months before and after present in data set

  JOIN months m2 ON date(m2.mth) = date(m1.mth, '-6 months')
  JOIN months m3 ON date(m3.mth) = date(m1.mth, '+6 months')
  GROUP BY m1.mth

rel_offsets AS (
  SELECT -6 AS off UNION ALL SELECT -5 UNION ALL SELECT -4 UNION ALL SELECT -3 UNION ALL
  SELECT -2 UNION ALL SELECT -1 UNION ALL SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL
  SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6
),

expanded AS (
  SELECT
    p.id AS product_id,
    tm.target_mth,
    date(tm.target_mth, printf('%+d months', ro.off)) AS member_mth,
    ro.off
  FROM target_months tm
  CROSS JOIN rel_offsets ro
  CROSS JOIN products p
),

expanded_with_qty AS (
  SELECT
    e.product_id,
    e.target_mth,
    e.member_mth,
    e.off,
    pms.qty

),

member_tagged AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    target_mth,
    member_mth,
    off,
    qty,
    CASE WHEN off BETWEEN -5 AND 6 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS in_winA,
    CASE WHEN off BETWEEN -6 AND 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS in_winB
  FROM expanded_with_qty
),

window_agg AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    target_mth,
    SUM(CASE WHEN in_winA=1 THEN COALESCE(qty,0) ELSE 0 END) AS winA_sum,
    SUM(CASE WHEN in_winA=1 THEN CASE WHEN qty IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END ELSE 0 END) AS winA_cnt,
    SUM(CASE WHEN in_winB=1 THEN COALESCE(qty,0) ELSE 0 END) AS winB_sum,
    SUM(CASE WHEN in_winB=1 THEN CASE WHEN qty IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END ELSE 0 END) AS winB_cnt,
    MAX(CASE WHEN off=0 THEN qty END) AS target_qty
  FROM member_tagged
  GROUP BY product_id, target_mth
),

cma AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    target_mth,
    target_qty,
    ( (winA_sum * 1.0) / 12.0 + (winB_sum * 1.0) / 12.0 ) / 2.0 AS cma
  FROM window_agg
  WHERE winA_cnt = 12 AND winB_cnt = 12
),

  SELECT

products_consistent AS (

FROM products_consistent pc

rows.question: Which customer has the highest average monthly change in payment amounts? Provide the customer's full name.

  SELECT

  f.arrival_airport,
  dep.city_en AS dep_city_en,
  arr.city_en AS arr_city_en,
  dep.longitude AS dep_longitude,
  dep.latitude AS dep_latitude,
  arr.longitude AS arr_longitude,
  arr.latitude AS arr_latitude
FROM flights_basic f

  AND arr.longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND arr.latitude IS NOT NULL

    ELSE v.arr_city_en

  CASE
    WHEN v.dep_city_en <= v.arr_city_en THEN v.arr_city_en
    ELSE v.dep_city_en
  END AS city_b_en,
  v.flight_id,
  -- Haversine formula to compute great-circle distance in kilometers
  -- coordinates: longitude and latitude in degrees
  ( 
    6371.0 * 2.0 * 
    ASIN(
      MIN(1.0,

          POWER(SIN(RADIANS((v.arr_latitude - v.dep_latitude) / 2.0)), 2)
          + COS(RADIANS(v.dep_latitude)) * COS(RADIANS(v.arr_latitude))

      WHEN avg_distance_km >= 2000 AND avg_distance_km < 3000 THEN '2000'
      WHEN avg_distance_km >= 3000 AND avg_distance_km < 4000 THEN '3000'
      WHEN avg_distance_km >= 4000 AND avg_distance_km < 5000 THEN '4000'
      WHEN avg_distance_km >= 5000 AND avg_distance_km < 6000 THEN '5000'
      ELSE '6000+'
    END AS bin_label,
    COUNT(*) AS pair_count
  FROM (
    SELECT city_a_en, city_b_en, AVG(flight_distance_km) AS avg_distance_km
    FROM city_pair_flight_distances
    GROUP BY city_a_en, city_b_en
  ) pair_avgs

rows.question: Considering only the customers who placed orders in 1998, calculate the total amount each customer spent by summing the unit price multiplied by the quantity of all products in their orders, excluding any discounts. rows.question: Can you provide the top 9 directors by movie count, including their ID, name, number of movies, average inter-movie duration (rounded to the nearest integer), average rating (rounded to 2 decimals), total votes, minimum and maximum ratings, and total movie duration? Sort the output first by movie count in descending order and then by total movie duration in descending order.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH movies_core AS (
  SELECT
    m.id AS id,
    m.title AS title,
    m.year AS year,
    m.duration AS duration
  FROM movies AS m
),
director_movie_link AS (
  SELECT
    dm.name_id AS director_id,
    n.name AS director_name,
    dm.movie_id AS movie_id,
    mc.year AS movie_year,
    mc.duration AS movie_duration
  FROM director_mapping dm
  JOIN names n ON n.id = dm.name_id
  JOIN movies_core mc ON mc.id = dm.movie_id
  WHERE mc.id IS NOT NULL
    AND n.id IS NOT NULL
),
movie_ratings AS (
  SELECT
    r.movie_id AS movie_id,
    r.avg_rating AS avg_rating,
    COALESCE(r.total_votes, 0) AS total_votes
  FROM ratings r
)
SELECT
  dml.director_id AS director_id,
  dml.director_name AS director_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT dml.movie_id) AS movie_count,
  CASE
    WHEN cnt_years.distinct_years_count < 2 THEN NULL
    ELSE ROUND(avgs.avg_diff)
  END AS avg_inter_movie_duration_years,
  ROUND(AVG(mr.avg_rating) FILTER (WHERE mr.avg_rating IS NOT NULL), 2) AS avg_rating,
  SUM(COALESCE(mr.total_votes, 0)) AS total_votes,
  MIN(mr.avg_rating) AS min_rating,
  MAX(mr.avg_rating) AS max_rating,
  SUM(COALESCE(dml.movie_duration, 0)) AS total_movie_duration
FROM director_movie_link dml
LEFT JOIN movie_ratings mr ON mr.movie_id = dml.movie_id
LEFT JOIN (
  -- average difference between consecutive distinct movie years per director
  SELECT director_id, AVG(year_diff) AS avg_diff
  FROM (
    SELECT director_id, (year_next - movie_year) AS year_diff
    FROM (
      SELECT director_id,
             movie_year,
             LEAD(movie_year) OVER (PARTITION BY director_id ORDER BY movie_year) AS year_next
      FROM (
        SELECT DISTINCT director_id, movie_year
        FROM director_movie_link
        WHERE movie_year IS NOT NULL
      ) AS distinct_years
    ) AS diffs
    WHERE year_next IS NOT NULL
  ) AS diffs_nonnull
  GROUP BY director_id
) AS avgs ON avgs.director_id = dml.director_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT director_id, COUNT(*) AS distinct_years_count
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT director_id, movie_year
    FROM director_movie_link
    WHERE movie_year IS NOT NULL
  ) AS d
  GROUP BY director_id
) AS cnt_years ON cnt_years.director_id = dml.director_id
GROUP BY dml.director_id, dml.director_name, avgs.avg_diff, cnt_years.distinct_years_count
ORDER BY movie_count DESC, total_movie_duration DESC

rows.question: Determine the top three genres with the most movies rated above 8, and then identify the top four directors who have directed the most films rated above 8 within those genres. List these directors and their respective movie counts.

),
movies_with_ratings AS (
  SELECT
    m.id AS id,
    r.avg_rating AS avg_rating
  FROM movies m
  JOIN ratings r ON m.id = r.movie_id
  WHERE r.avg_rating > 8.0
),
top3_genres AS (
  SELECT
    g.genre
  FROM genre g
  JOIN movies_with_ratings mwr ON g.movie_id = mwr.id
  GROUP BY g.genre
  ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT mwr.id) DESC, g.genre
  LIMIT 3
),
-- Counts for the top 3 genres
genre_counts AS (
  SELECT
    tg.genre AS genre,
    COUNT(DISTINCT g.movie_id) AS movie_count_above_8

  JOIN genre g ON g.genre = tg.genre
  JOIN movies_with_ratings mwr ON g.movie_id = mwr.id

    m.winner_id AS winner_id,
